Ellen Park: Heads-up: legal asked for an operator-playbook for multi-region fallback events that may move EU tenant data. We don't have a clear chain-of-custody today. Can we define one?

Diego Silva: Short version: introduce a three-mode fallback contract for the runtime: DENY, ESCROW, and ALLOW. DENY = reject any cross-region routing; ESCROW = forward encrypted envelope only; ALLOW = full forward.

Nora Khan: +1 but we need to be concrete about who can trigger ESCROW unwraps and how to record approvals. Suggestion: a mandatory approval record (operator id, justification, timestamp) and an immutable envelope manifest stored in WORM storage.

Ellen Park: How will the proxy decide? We need a reliable source of truth: tenant config in control plane (not headers). Proxy can accept a header X-Requested-Residency but must validate against control-plane policy.

Diego Silva: Implementation sketch:
1) proxy receives request, looks up tenant.config.residency and tenant.policy
2) if region mismatch and policy==DENY -> 409 with code residency.violation
3) if policy==ESCROW -> proxy wraps payload: AES-GCM encrypt, KMS-wrap key, write envelope to escrow-store, tag telemetry "escrow_created", forward envelope-ref to target region
4) target region requests unwrap -> control plane checks tenant.fallback_approval and RBAC; if allowed, KMS unwrap returns ephemeral key and target decrypts. Every unwrap event writes immutable audit record.

ops-bot: deploy: residency-guard v0.3 pushed to canary (eu-1) at 2024-08-20T17:03:00Z

Nora Khan: For scale: automatic unwrap only when tenant.fallback_approval==true and tenant.sla_tier==enterprise. Otherwise manual approval via operator UI which records approver + justification and triggers KMS unwrap with HSM-backed key.

Ellen Park: Retention: logs/audit trail must be kept 7 years. Escrow payloads themselves default to 90 days unless legal hold. We should offer an "archive" flag per-tenant to keep payloads longer (cost + privacy implications).

Diego Silva: Performance note: adding AES+KMS wrap adds ~4ms on warm path with HW accel; on CPU nodes under load p95 can be +20-30ms. We'll bind ESCROW to SLA tiers to avoid p99 regressions for free-tier customers.

Nora Khan: Telemetry keys to add: residency.fallback_attempt, residency.fallback_mode, escrow.envelope_size_bytes, escrow.kms_wrap_ms, escrow.unwrap_attempts, escrow.unwrap_approved. Tag by tenant.region, tenant.id, and route.

security-agent: Security checklist: ephemeral keys must never be logged; KMS access audited; escrow-store encrypted server-side and write-once enabled; operator unwrap requires two-person approval for EU tenants unless tenant opted-in.

Ellen Park: Runbook sketch:
- Step 1: proxy detects fallback attempt -> emit alert + create "residency-fallback" incident in lightweight mode
- Step 2: if policy==DENY -> incident auto-resolve with metrics + customer notif
- Step 3: if policy==ESCROW and tenant.auto_unwrap==false -> page oncall; oncall opens operator UI, reviews envelope, records approval -> unwrap proceeds
- Step 4: escalate to legal for any unusual unwraps or if customer requests audit transcript

Diego Silva: Action items: Diego -> PR for proxy changes (header validation + escrow envelope format); Nora -> operator UI mockups with approval workflow; Ellen -> update privacy/SLA docs and retention table; Security -> finalize RBAC + HSM gating.

Ellen Park: Agreed. Also: include a compact signed manifest with every envelope so we can prove chain-of-custody to auditors.
